Mahākāśyapa.question: Some Chinese and _____ texts state that there was "doubt and consternation" among many disciples
Mahākāśyapa.fact: Some Chinese and Tibetan texts state that there was "doubt and consternation" among many disciples.

Mahākāśyapa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahākāśyapa.question: The Sanskrit Aśokavadāna and the _____āprajñāpāramitāśāstra say that many enlightened disciples wished to stop teaching, leave the world behind and attain paranirvāṇa
Mahākāśyapa.fact: The Sanskrit Aśokavadāna and the Chinese Mahāprajñāpāramitāśāstra say that many enlightened disciples wished to stop teaching, leave the world behind and attain paranirvāṇa.

Mahākāśyapa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahākāśyapa.question: According to the texts, the _____ was held in a cave called Saptaparṇaguhā in Rājagṛha (Pali: Sattapaṇṇaguhā; Rājagaha, present-day Rajgir), which was the site of many Buddhist discourses
Mahākāśyapa.fact: To record the Buddha's discourses and preserve monastic discipline, Mahākāśyapa set up the First Buddhist Council. According to the texts, the First Buddhist Council was held in a cave called Saptaparṇaguhā in Rājagṛha (Pali: Sattapaṇṇaguhā; Rājagaha, present-day Rajgir), which was the site of many Buddhist discourses.

Mahākāśyapa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahākāśyapa.question: Then the assembly agreed that Ānanda's memories and recitations were correct, after which the discourse collection (_____: Sūtra Piṭaka, Pali: Sutta Piṭaka) was considered finalized and closed
Mahākāśyapa.fact: Then the assembly agreed that Ānanda's memories and recitations were correct, after which the discourse collection (Sanskrit: Sūtra Piṭaka, Pali: Sutta Piṭaka) was considered finalized and closed.

Mahākāśyapa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahākāśyapa.question: In some versions of the account, the _____ (Pali: Abhidhamma) was also standardized during this council, or rather its precursor the Mātṛka
Mahākāśyapa.fact: In some versions of the account, the Abhidharma (Pali: Abhidhamma) was also standardized during this council, or rather its precursor the Mātṛka.

Mahākāśyapa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahākāśyapa.question: Before the _____'s parinirvāṇa, he had mentioned to Ānanda that, if required, minor rules could be abolished after his death
Mahākāśyapa.fact: Before the Buddha's parinirvāṇa, he had mentioned to Ānanda that, if required, minor rules could be abolished after his death. Now the question remained what the Buddha had meant when he said minor rules.

Mahākāśyapa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahākāśyapa.question: Now the question remained what the _____ had meant when he said minor rules
Mahākāśyapa.fact: Before the Buddha's parinirvāṇa, he had mentioned to Ānanda that, if required, minor rules could be abolished after his death. Now the question remained what the Buddha had meant when he said minor rules.

Mahākāśyapa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahākāśyapa.question: However, texts of the _____āstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, and Mahīśāsaka traditions relate that this was Ājñāta Kauṇḍinya (Pali: Añña-Koṇḍañña) instead, as Kauṇḍinya was the most senior disciple
Mahākāśyapa.fact: However, texts of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, and Mahīśāsaka traditions relate that this was Ājñāta Kauṇḍinya (Pali: Añña-Koṇḍañña) instead, as Kauṇḍinya was the most senior disciple.

Mahākāśyapa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahākāśyapa.question: Buddhologist Jean Przyluski (_____–1944) argued that the earliest accounts placed Kauṇḍinya at the head of the saṃgha, and that originally, Mahākāśyapa was a conventional figure, with no administrativ
Mahākāśyapa.fact: Buddhologist Jean Przyluski (1885–1944) argued that the earliest accounts placed Kauṇḍinya at the head of the saṃgha, and that originally, Mahākāśyapa was a conventional figure, with no administrative or leading role.

Mahākāśyapa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahākāśyapa.question: Tradition states that the _____ lasted for seven months
Mahākāśyapa.fact: Tradition states that the First Council lasted for seven months. However, many scholars, from the late 19th century onward, have considered the historicity of the First Council improbable.

Mahākāśyapa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahākāśyapa.question: However, many scholars, from the late 19th century onward, have considered the historicity of the _____ improbable
Mahākāśyapa.fact: Tradition states that the First Council lasted for seven months. However, many scholars, from the late 19th century onward, have considered the historicity of the First Council improbable.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: The _____ was Foster mother of Gautama Buddha and the first Buddhist nun.
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī (Sanskrit: महाप्रजापती गौतमी; Pali: Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī) or simply Prajāpatī was the foster-mother, step-mother and maternal aunt (mother's sister) of the Buddha.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: In _____ tradition, she was the first woman to seek ordination for women, which she did from Siddhartha Gautama directly, and she became the first bhikṣuṇī (Buddhist nun)
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: In Buddhist tradition, she was the first woman to seek ordination for women, which she did from Siddhartha Gautama directly, and she became the first bhikṣuṇī (Buddhist nun).

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: It is recorded in the various surviving Vinaya traditions, including the _____ and Sarvastivada and Mulasarvastivada versions
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: It is recorded in the various surviving Vinaya traditions, including the Pali Canon and Sarvastivada and Mulasarvastivada versions.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: The stories of her past lives are included in the Therīgāthā, Theri-apadāna and _____
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: The stories of her past lives are included in the Therīgāthā, Theri-apadāna and Jataka.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: She witnessed _____ place his aunt, a bhikkhuni, in a senior position, and aspired to achieve the same position after providing offerings to the Buddha and his followers for seven days
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: She witnessed Padumuttara Buddha place his aunt, a bhikkhuni, in a senior position, and aspired to achieve the same position after providing offerings to the Buddha and his followers for seven days.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: She was later reborn in the _____ heaven as a god
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: She was later reborn in the Tavatimsa heaven as a god.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: Following the rain retreat, _____ī had her followers prepare robes for the paccekabuddhas
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: Gotamī then returned to the human realm as the leader of 500 female slaves. Gotamī asked the 500 female slaves to provide food offerings and convinced their husbands to build huts for the rain retreat.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: In another rebirth, Gotamī is said to have given food alms to 500 paccekabuddhas near _____
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: In another rebirth, Gotamī is said to have given food alms to 500 paccekabuddhas near Varanasi.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: Gotamī and her followers continued to perform meritorious acts throughout their lives and were reborn as _____ gods
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: Gotamī and her followers continued to perform meritorious acts throughout their lives and were reborn as Tavatimsa gods.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: Gotamī's followers would follow her in each birth and attain liberation as bhikkhunis during the time of _____
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: Gotamī's followers would follow her in each birth and attain liberation as bhikkhunis during the time of Gautama Buddha.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: Mahāpajāpatī was both the _____'s maternal aunt and adoptive mother, raising him after her sister Maya, the Buddha's birth mother, died
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: In another rebirth, Gotamī is said to have given food alms to 500 paccekabuddhas near Varanasi. Gotamī's followers would follow her in each birth and attain liberation as bhikkhunis during the time of Gautama Buddha.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: She raised _____ as if he were her own child
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: She raised Siddhartha as if he were her own child.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: An eminent Therī, Mahāpajāpatī was born at _____ as the younger sister of Māyā
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: An eminent Therī, Mahāpajāpatī was born at Devdaha as the younger sister of Māyā.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: Both sisters married _____, leader of the Śākya
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: Both sisters married King Suddhodhana, leader of the Śākya.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: When Māyā died seven days after the birth of the _____ (the "Buddha-to-be"), Pajāpati looked after the Bodhisatta and nursed him
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: When Māyā died seven days after the birth of the Bodhisatta (the "Buddha-to-be"), Pajāpati looked after the Bodhisatta and nursed him.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: She raised the _____ and had her own children, Siddhartha's half-sister Sundari Nanda and half-brother Nanda
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: When Māyā died seven days after the birth of the Bodhisatta (the "Buddha-to-be"), Pajāpati looked after the Bodhisatta and nursed him. She raised the Buddha and had her own children, Siddhartha's half-sister Sundari Nanda and half-brother Nanda.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: Gotamī went to the _____ and asked to be ordained into the Sangha three times
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: When Māyā died seven days after the birth of the Bodhisatta (the "Buddha-to-be"), Pajāpati looked after the Bodhisatta and nursed him. She raised the Buddha and had her own children, Siddhartha's half-sister Sundari Nanda and half-brother Nanda.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: Undaunted, Gotamī cut off her hair and donned yellow robes and with 500 princesses, 250 from the Sakyan kingdom and 250 from the _____ kingdom followed the Buddha to Vesāli on foot
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: Undaunted, Gotamī cut off her hair and donned yellow robes and with 500 princesses, 250 from the Sakyan kingdom and 250 from the Koliyan kingdom followed the Buddha to Vesāli on foot.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: Upon arrival, Gotamī stood crying at the entrance of the _____'s residence
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: Gotamī went to the Buddha and asked to be ordained into the Sangha three times. The Buddha refused and went on to Vesāli.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: Ananda, one of the principal disciples and an attendant of the _____, met her and offered to intercede with the Buddha on her behalf
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: The Buddha refused and went on to Vesāli. Undaunted, Gotamī cut off her hair and donned yellow robes and with 500 princesses, 250 from the Sakyan kingdom and 250 from the Koliyan kingdom followed the Buddha to Vesāli on foot.

Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.question: "If that is so, Lord, then it would be good if women could be ordained as nuns," said _____, encouraged by the Buddha's reply
Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī.fact: Ananda, one of the principal disciples and an attendant of the Buddha, met her and offered to intercede with the Buddha on her behalf. Ananda was refused the first two times and asked the following in this third attempt: Respectfully he questioned the Buddha, "Lord, are women capable of realising the various stages of sainthood as nuns?" "They are, Ananda," said the Buddha.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: The _____ was Historical chronicle of Sri Lanka.
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: Mahāvaṃsa (Pali: මහාවංස, romanized: Mahāvaṃsa) is the historical chronicle of Sri Lanka until the period of Mahasena of Anuradhapura.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: It was written in the style of an epic poem written in the _____ language
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: Mahāvaṃsa (Pali: මහාවංස, romanized: Mahāvaṃsa) is the historical chronicle of Sri Lanka until the period of Mahasena of Anuradhapura. It was written in the style of an epic poem written in the Pali language.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: It was first composed by a _____ monk named Mahānāma at the Mahavihāraya Temple in Anuradhapura in the 5th or 6th-century
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: It was first composed by a Buddhist monk named Mahānāma at the Mahavihāraya Temple in Anuradhapura in the 5th or 6th-century.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: Eugène Burnouf produced a Romanized transliteration and translation into Latin in _____, but these garnered relatively little attention
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: Eugène Burnouf produced a Romanized transliteration and translation into Latin in 1826, but these garnered relatively little attention.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: The first printed edition and widely read English translation was published in _____ by George Turnour, a historian and officer of the Ceylon Civil Service who translated 38 chapters
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: The first printed edition and widely read English translation was published in 1837 by George Turnour, a historian and officer of the Ceylon Civil Service who translated 38 chapters.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: Louis Corneille Wijesinghe completed the remaining 62 chapters and reviewed Turnour's work, publishing in _____
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: Louis Corneille Wijesinghe completed the remaining 62 chapters and reviewed Turnour's work, publishing in 1889.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: A German translation of the Mahavamsa was completed by Wilhelm Geiger in _____
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: A German translation of the Mahavamsa was completed by Wilhelm Geiger in 1912.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: This was then translated into English by _____, and revised by Geiger
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: This was then translated into English by Mabel Haynes Bode, and revised by Geiger.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: In _____, the Mahāvaṃsa was listed an item of globally important documentary heritage on UNESCO’s Memory of the World Programme's International Register
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: In 2023, the Mahāvaṃsa was listed an item of globally important documentary heritage on UNESCO’s Memory of the World Programme's International Register.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: These annals were then combined and compiled into a single document in the 5th century while _____ was ruling the Anuradhapura Kingdom
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: These annals were then combined and compiled into a single document in the 5th century while King Dhatusena was ruling the Anuradhapura Kingdom.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: It was written based on prior ancient compilations known as the _____ (sometimes Sinhalaatthakatha), which were commentaries written in Sinhala
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: It was written based on prior ancient compilations called the Atthakatha (sometimes Sinhalaatthakatha), which were commentaries written in Sinhala. An earlier document called the Dipavamsa (4th century CE) "Chronicles of the Island" is much simpler and contains less information than the Mahavamsa and was probably compiled using the Atthakatha on the Mahavamsa as well.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: Authorship of the _____ is attributed to an otherwise unknown monk called Mahānāma by the Mahavamsa-tika
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: An earlier document called the Dipavamsa (4th century CE) "Chronicles of the Island" is much simpler and contains less information than the Mahavamsa and was probably compiled using the Atthakatha on the Mahavamsa as well. Authorship of the Mahavamsa is attributed to an otherwise unknown monk called Mahānāma by the Mahavamsa-tika.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: Mahānāma is described as residing in a monastery belonging to general _____ and affiliated with the Mahavihara, but no other reliable biographical information is known
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: Mahānāma is described as residing in a monastery belonging to general Dighasanda and affiliated with the Mahavihara, but no other reliable biographical information is known.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: These visits are not mentioned in the _____ or other early sources
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: These visits are not mentioned in the Pali Canon or other early sources.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: Chronicles of Kings of _____: This material consists of genealogies and lineages of Sri Lankan kings, sometimes with stories about their succession or notable incidents in their reigns
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: These stories describe the Buddha subduing or driving away the Yakkhas (Yakshas) and Nagas that were inhabiting the island and delivering a prophecy that Sri Lanka will become an important Buddhist center. Chronicles of Kings of Sri Lanka: This material consists of genealogies and lineages of Sri Lankan kings, sometimes with stories about their succession or notable incidents in their reigns.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: History of the _____: This section of the Mahavamsa deals with the mission sent by Emperor Ashoka to Sri Lanka, the transplantation of the bodhi tree, and the founding of the Mahavihara
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: History of the Buddhist Sangha: This section of the Mahavamsa deals with the mission sent by Emperor Ashoka to Sri Lanka, the transplantation of the bodhi tree, and the founding of the Mahavihara.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: It includes the names of prominent monks and nuns in the early _____ sangha
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: Chronicles of Kings of Sri Lanka: This material consists of genealogies and lineages of Sri Lankan kings, sometimes with stories about their succession or notable incidents in their reigns. It includes the names of prominent monks and nuns in the early Sri Lankan sangha.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: It also includes accounts of the early _____ councils and the first recording of the Pali canon in writing
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: History of the Buddhist Sangha: This section of the Mahavamsa deals with the mission sent by Emperor Ashoka to Sri Lanka, the transplantation of the bodhi tree, and the founding of the Mahavihara. It also includes accounts of the early Buddhist councils and the first recording of the Pali canon in writing.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: It is one of the few documents containing material relating to the Nāga and _____ peoples, indigenous inhabitants of Lanka before the legendary arrival of Prince Vijaya from Singha Pura of Kalinga
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: It is one of the few documents containing material relating to the Nāga and Yakkha peoples, indigenous inhabitants of Lanka before the legendary arrival of Prince Vijaya from Singha Pura of Kalinga.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: As it often refers to the royal dynasties of India, the _____ is also valuable for historians who wish to date and relate contemporary royal dynasties in the Indian subcontinent
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: The combined work sometimes referred to collectively as the Mahavamsa, provides a continuous historical record of over two millennia, and is considered one of the world's longest unbroken historical accounts. As it often refers to the royal dynasties of India, the Mahavamsa is also valuable for historians who wish to date and relate contemporary royal dynasties in the Indian subcontinent.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: It is very important in dating the consecration of the _____, which is related to the synchronicity with the Seleucid Empire and Alexander the Great
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: It is very important in dating the consecration of the Maurya Emperor Ashoka, which is related to the synchronicity with the Seleucid Empire and Alexander the Great.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: Indian excavations in _____ and other locations, confirm the Mahavamsa account of the empire of Ashoka
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: Indian excavations in Sanchi and other locations, confirm the Mahavamsa account of the empire of Ashoka.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: The accounts given in the _____ are also amply supported by the numerous stone inscriptions, mostly in Sinhala, found in Sri Lanka
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: As it often refers to the royal dynasties of India, the Mahavamsa is also valuable for historians who wish to date and relate contemporary royal dynasties in the Indian subcontinent. Indian excavations in Sanchi and other locations, confirm the Mahavamsa account of the empire of Ashoka.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: K. _____ has also upheld the historical value of the Mahavamsa
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: K. Indrapala has also upheld the historical value of the Mahavamsa.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: As a result of the _____, comparatively more is known about the history of the island of Sri Lanka and neighboring regions than that of most of the subcontinent
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: The accounts given in the Mahavamsa are also amply supported by the numerous stone inscriptions, mostly in Sinhala, found in Sri Lanka. K. Indrapala has also upheld the historical value of the Mahavamsa.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: The Mahamvasa covers the early history of Buddhism in _____, beginning with the time of Siddhartha Gautama, the founder of Buddhism
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: If not for the Mahavamsa, the story behind the large stupas in Anuradhapura, Sri Lanka, such as Ruwanwelisaya, Jetavanaramaya, Abhayagiri vihāra and other works of ancient engineering would never have been known. As a result of the Mahavamsa, comparatively more is known about the history of the island of Sri Lanka and neighboring regions than that of most of the subcontinent.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: It also briefly recounts the history of _____ in India, from the date of the Buddha's death to the 3rd Buddhist council where the Dharma was reviewed
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: Its contents have aided in the identification and corroboration of archaeological sites and inscriptions associated with early Buddhism, the empire of Ashoka, and even the Tamil kingdoms of southern India. The Mahamvasa covers the early history of Buddhism in Sri Lanka, beginning with the time of Siddhartha Gautama, the founder of Buddhism.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: Every chapter of the _____ ends by stating that it is written for the "serene joy of the pious"
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: Every chapter of the Mahavamsa ends by stating that it is written for the "serene joy of the pious". Besides being an important historical source, the Mahavamsa is the most important epic poem in the Pali language.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: Besides being an important historical source, the _____ is the most important epic poem in the Pali language
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: Every chapter of the Mahavamsa ends by stating that it is written for the "serene joy of the pious". Besides being an important historical source, the Mahavamsa is the most important epic poem in the Pali language.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: From the emphasis of its point-of-view, and being compiled to record the good deeds of the kings who were patrons of the _____, it has been said to support Sinhalese nationalism
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: From the emphasis of its point-of-view, and being compiled to record the good deeds of the kings who were patrons of the Anuradhapura Maha Viharaya, it has been said to support Sinhalese nationalism.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: Unlike many texts written in antiquity, it also discusses various aspects of the lives of ordinary people, and how they joined the _____'s army or farmed
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: From the emphasis of its point-of-view, and being compiled to record the good deeds of the kings who were patrons of the Anuradhapura Maha Viharaya, it has been said to support Sinhalese nationalism. Unlike many texts written in antiquity, it also discusses various aspects of the lives of ordinary people, and how they joined the King's army or farmed.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: Thus the _____ was taken along the Silk Road to many Buddhist lands
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: Besides being an important historical source, the Mahavamsa is the most important epic poem in the Pali language. Thus the Mahavamsa was taken along the Silk Road to many Buddhist lands.

Mahāvaṃsa.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Mahāvaṃsa.question: An extended version of the _____, which gives many more details, has also been found in Southeast Asia
Mahāvaṃsa.fact: Thus the Mahavamsa was taken along the Silk Road to many Buddhist lands. An extended version of the Mahavamsa, which gives many more details, has also been found in Southeast Asia.
